subject.name_or_desc: A woman, at Lilly's house in the country

context.question: Is my son with his master, or at my own house?
context.asked_at: Question figure discussed as of July 1638 (figure heading in the 1647 printing is partly illegible in OCR: 'Anno Dom. 1638 ... July'); Lilly computed from the ephemeris that the significators of mother and son perfected a trine on 25 July at 2 p.m.
context.setting: Her son was away from home; she did not know where he was staying

attachments.asc_ruler: Venus (lady of the ascendant, significator of the querent/mother)
attachments.key_positions: Jupiter, lord of the 5th (the son's significator), placed in the Ascendant (east angle); Moon in 27° Pisces applying to a sextile of Saturn, lord of the 4th (the mother's dwelling); Mars lord of the 6th in Sagittarius; the absent party also described by Jupiter in the Ascendant and Venus in the 9th
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; the full figure is printed as Fig. 3 in the 1852 edition and in Book II of the 1647 original.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.edition: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition where noted
provenance.page: Book II, the example figure resolving four queries (1st: if a party might be found at home; 4th: if one absent be dead or alive) — 1647 pp.190ff in modern reprint pagination; Fig. 3 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition

context.question: (1) Shall I be rich, or subsist of myself without marriage? (2) By what means shall I attain wealth? (3) When? (4) Shall it continue?
context.asked_at: 1634, London (exact day not stated in the text)
context.setting: Asked in the year 1634; Lilly lived to see the outcome ('I have seen the experience of my judgment')

attachments.asc_ruler: Venus, lady of the ascendant, near Regulus (Cor Leonis)
attachments.key_positions: Mars, lord of the 2nd and lord of the Part of Fortune, in the Ascendant near Spica at 18° Libra; Jupiter in his exaltation (Cancer) angular, almost culminating (10th); Moon lady of the 10th in Leo, separating from sextile of Mars and conjunction of Mercury, applying to conjunction of Venus, wanting 6°27' of the conjunction; Part of Fortune in a fixed sign in the terms of Mars; cusp of the 2nd a fixed sign
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.edition: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition where noted
provenance.page: Book II, chapter on 2nd-house questions (whether the querent shall be rich), example figure of the London tradesman

subject.name_or_desc: A master whose servant (a young fellow of about nineteen) had run away the Sunday preceding

context.question: Which way is the fugitive servant gone, and when shall he return / be recovered?
context.asked_at: Not stated in the text (servant left on the Sunday before the question)
context.setting: The servant had left his master and his whereabouts were unknown

attachments.key_positions: Ascendant with its lord and the Moon therein signifying the master; Mercury peculiarly the servant's significator in this figure (the Moon being the common significator of servants); Moon at the time of flight in a western sign and still in the same sign; Mercury in a western sign, south quarter; Moon in the 2nd in her own house; Sun in the 2nd in perfect aspect with a planet in the 11th; servant's significator and lord of the Ascendant hastening to a trine out of angles
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.edition: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition where noted
provenance.page: Book II, Chap. LXI 'Of Fugitive Servant, which way gone, when return'

subject.name_or_desc: A lady who had long been courted by a gentleman suitor; she had continually slighted him and finally given him an absolute denial, then bitterly repented and wished the match revived

context.question: Can this marriage match be revived/effected?
context.asked_at: June of an unstated year (Lilly advised the gentleman to make the first move on 19 June near noon; Saturn and Mars came to aspect on 27 June)
context.setting: She came to Lilly in great heaviness, asking whether the match could be brought on again without scandal to her honour; Lilly first read her own history from the figure, which she then confessed in full

attachments.key_positions: Sun, lord of the Ascendant, significator of the lady; Saturn, lord of the 7th, significator of the gentleman, in the south angle in conjunction with Mars in a fixed earthy sign, elevated; Moon separated from [the gentleman's significator] void of course, applying to opposition of the Sun; reception between Venus and the Moon, and between the Sun and Venus; Moon disposing of Saturn in her exaltation; Jupiter in his exaltation applying to a sextile of Saturn, lord of the 7th, and transferring Saturn's virtue to the Sun, lord of the Ascendant, with no prohibition, abscission or frustration before the aspect perfected (perfected 27 June)
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.edition: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition where noted
provenance.page: Book II, 7th-house (marriage) chapters — the example judgment printed at 1647 pp.385–388, immediately before Chap. LXI

subject.name_or_desc: A querent whose money had been stolen; he suspected a woman servant (shown by Mars) and another (shown by Saturn) and tried to persuade Lilly of it

context.question: Who stole my money, and shall I have it again?
context.setting: Question of theft: who is the thief, and shall the money be recovered?

attachments.key_positions: Mars, lord of the Ascendant, in 25°02' Leo, in square to Mercury and Saturn, but in his own terms and face (therefore refused as the thief's significator); Saturn in the west angle (7th, house of theft) likewise in his own term and face (also passed by); Mercury in an angle, having no essential dignity, in partile conjunction with Saturn and square to Mars — taken to signify the thief; Moon in a masculine sign applying to Mars; Mercury conjunct Saturn and square Mars, both masculine planets; Moon so near the Sun, separating
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment (Fig. 18 in the 1852 edition).

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.edition: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition where noted
provenance.page: Book II, theft chapters — judgment on Fig. 18 (wording cross-checked in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
